EK card ^kzr7way adds the modifier, on EditorKit main bab334ea. + +## The rule +- A native control keeps the system focus and selection look. +- A kit item (card, chip, row, tile) shows its state as a fill in its own shape, with no outline: a soft accent fill when selected, a stronger accent fill when its scope holds the focus, and grey when the window is not key. +- An item with a surface shows no scope focus ring. An area with no surface (a panel, a list) keeps its ring. +- The reference look is the selected PathChip in the SVK gallery (shared-path-chip-change). + +## The EK API (EditorCommandsUI, Sources/EditorCommandsUI/SelectableItem.swift) +- `.selectableItem(isSelected: Bool, radius: EditorStyle.Radius)` and `.selectableItem(isSelected: Bool, cornerRadius: CGFloat)`. Put it INSIDE the `.commandScope` of the item. It draws the fill (selected: accent at `EditorStyle.selectionOpacity`; scope holds focus: accent at `EditorStyle.focusedSelectionOpacity`; window not key: grey), sets the hit and focus shape in the same corners, and tells the enclosing scope to draw no ring. +- `\.commandScopeHoldsFocus` (read only). +- `\.isItemStateFillShown` (EditorStyle, read only): a base fill of an item goes INSIDE `.selectableItem` and draws nothing while it is true. + +## Changes in AgentViewKit +Step 0: Update the EditorKit pin to bab334ea or later in the root package, IntegrationTests and ScreenshotTests (`swift package --package-path

update EditorKit`). Package.resolved is git-ignored. + +1. Keep one way for kits: `.selectableSurface(_:corners:)` and `.selectableSurface(_:radius:)` of AgentViewKitStyle (Sources/AgentViewKitStyle/Theme/SelectableSurface.swift) wrap `.selectableItem(isSelected:cornerRadius:)` with the radius of the corners. They keep working for an item with no scope (a gallery sample). AgentViewKitStyle may need the EditorCommandsUI product: check Package.swift (`styleEditorKitProducts`) and add it if necessary. If the dependency is not acceptable in the style target, record the reason on this card and use the other way (replace `.selectableSurface` with `.selectableItem` at each use site). +2. Every selectable item of AVK must have its surface modifier INSIDE its `.commandScope`, and must not add `.scopeFocusRing` on top. Check each site: + - Sources/AgentViewKit/Lists/AgentRowList.swift:586-588 (row: `.selectableSurface` is outside the scope now through `wrappedSurface`? check the order; remove `.scopeFocusRing(radius:)` of the row). The list area at :331-332 has no surface: it keeps its ring. + - Sources/AgentViewKit/Commands/AgentItemScope.swift:59-61 (message rows, permission request cards, tool call cards, attachment items through AgentAttachmentScope). An item with a surface removes `.scopeFocusRing`, and shows focus as the stronger fill (`.selectableItem(isSelected: false, ...)` inside the scope if the item is not selectable). An item with no surface keeps the ring. + - Sources/AgentViewKit/Elicitation/ElicitationTabChip.swift:43, Sources/AgentViewKit/Diff/DiffView.swift:245, Sources/AgentViewKit/Attachments/AttachmentView.swift:237, Sources/AgentViewKitStyle/Theme/SelectableSurface.swift:117. + - Sources/AgentViewKit/Commands/AgentControlScope.swift:70-72: native controls keep the system focus look. Do not change unless the control draws its own item surface. +3. A base fill of an item (a card background) goes INSIDE the selection modifier and reads `\.isItemStateFillShown`, so no two fills stack. +4. Update the doc comments that talk about the focus ring of items (for example AgentItemScope, SelectableSurface). +5. Tests: update the tests that check the focus ring of an item. Add a test that a focused item with a surface draws no scope ring. Test rules: no clock/sleep/poll/retry/timeLimit/XCUITest; tests never show a window or take focus. +6. Record all the screenshots again (`swift test --package-path ScreenshotTests`) and give the changed PNG paths to the user. + +## Acceptance criteria +- A selected item shows the soft accent fill. A focused item shows the stronger fill. Inactive window: grey. No outline on items with a surface. +- Lists and panels with no surface keep their ring. Native controls do not change. +- All unit, integration and screenshot tests pass. +- The snapshot images are new, and the user has the paths. + +Commit only. Do not push: the user of AVK decides the push. \ No newline at end of file

+  text: |-
+    Research results:
+    - EditorSwiftUI of EK already depends on EditorCommandsUI. Thus the EditorCommandsUI product in AgentViewKitStyle adds no new package to the closure of the style target (no ACP product). It is acceptable: step 1 uses the first way (`.selectableSurface` wraps `.selectableItem`).
+    - EK scope: `showsRing = holdsFocus && !hasItemSurface`. The `ScopeItemSurfaceKey` preference goes to the NEAREST enclosing scope. Thus a `.selectableItem` on a part with no scope of its own (the file chips of DiffView, the tab chips of an elicitation) goes to the scope around it (for example a tool call), removes the ring of that scope, and fills each chip with the focus fill of that scope. These parts must show the selection only: they use a selection-only form (EK `.selectionSurface` with the hit shape), not `.selectableItem`.
+    - Items with no surface (no edge, no fill): message rows, tool call tiles, the attachment inspector panel. They keep the scope ring.
+    - Items with a surface: AgentRowList rows, the permission card (edge), the AttachmentChip (base fill), file views with `InspectorSelectable` (AttachmentView, ImageView, location chips). ArtifactView (edge) holds an AttachmentView of the same attachment with no scope of its own: that file view is the item surface of the shared scope. A second fill on the artifact card would stack on it.
+    - The permission card is focusable (`@FocusState`, `.focusEffectDisabled()`): a landing gives the focus to the card, not to the beacon, so `\.commandScopeHoldsFocus` is false and the card shows `.editorFocusRing`. EK permits this ring for a focusable card. EK has no public API to draw the focused fill from the focus of a focusable view (`selectableItemSurface(isSelected:isFocused:cornerRadius:)` is `package`).
